heading: INT. HOSPITAL STAIRWELL - LANDING BETWEEN FLOORS - 3 A.M.

units.text: INT. HOSPITAL STAIRWELL - LANDING BETWEEN FLOORS - 3 A.M.
Concrete steps.
A humming exit sign.
A window onto a dark parking structure.
A vending machine glows at the landing.
DR. ANSELMO KWAKU-REYNOLDS, 40s, scrubs, paper hat crumpled in his fist, sits on the steps with his head against the wall.
A phone rests on his knee, speaker on.
Cardiology to Dr. Kwaku-Reynolds. Please call extension four-four-one-two.
units.name: OPERATOR

units.text: I'm on a break.
units.name: ANSELMO

units.text: Doctor, they said it's urgent.
units.name: OPERATOR

units.text: It's always urgent.
units.name: ANSELMO

units.text: He turns the phone face down on the step.
The voice continues in muffled bursts.
He lets it.
Forty-one patients on the unit. Three discharges at eight. Two transfers at noon. One bed that nobody gets until I sign off on a chart I haven't finished. And I'm sitting on a stair.
units.name: ANSELMO

units.text: He laughs, quietly.
Wipes a hand over his face.
When I was a student, an old attending told me: "A doctor is a man who fixes what he can and carries what he can't." I thought it was poetry.
units.name: ANSELMO

units.text: A pause.
The vending machine hums.
It's a weight limit.
units.name: ANSELMO

units.text: He stands, brushes off his scrubs, flattens the paper hat, puts it on.
Picks up the phone.
This is Kwaku-Reynolds. Coming up.
units.name: ANSELMO

units.text: Thank you, Doctor.
units.name: OPERATOR

units.text: He pockets the phone and climbs.
